'''Chiang Chung''' "'''CC'''" '''Mei''' ({{Lang-zh|t=梅強中}}; April 4, 1935 – July 16, 2026) was a Taiwanese-American physicist who was the Ford Professor of Engineering Emeritus at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT). He is known for his contributions in [[fluid mechanics]] with applications to [[civil engineering|civil]], [[environmental engineering|environmental]], and [[coastal engineering]].

==Early life and education==
Mei was born in [[Wuchang, Wuhan]], China on April 4, 1935.<ref name="death">{{cite web |title=Chiang Chung Mei |url=https://www.joycefuneralhome.com/obituaries/chiang-mei |website=Joyce Funeral Home |access-date=18 July 2026}}</ref> He received his [[B.S.]] (1955) from [[National Taiwan University]], [[M.S.]] (1958) from [[Stanford University]], and [[Ph.D.]] (1963) from [[California Institute of Technology]].

==Career==
Mei was an associate editor of the ''[[Journal of Fluid Mechanics]]''. He received the Moffatt–Nichol Award in 1992 and the International Coastal Engineering Award in 1995, both from the [[American Society of Civil Engineers]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Awards and Honours |date=November 15, 1995 |journal=MIT News |url=https://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/1995/awards12-1115.html |accessdate=2011-01-15}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Theodore von Karman Medal]] in 2007.

The 24th International Workshop on Water Waves and Floating Bodies of 2009 was dedicated to Mei on the occasion of his retirement.<ref>{{Citation |title=Proceedings of the 24th International Workshop on Water Waves and Floating Bodies |df=mdy-all |year=2009 |editor-last=Plotnikov |editor-first=Pavel |url=http://www.iwwwfb.org/Abstracts/iwwwfb24/iwwwfb24_00.pdf |url-status=dead |place=Zelenogorsk |editor2-last=Korobkin |editor2-first=Alexander |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726200757/http://www.iwwwfb.org/Abstracts/iwwwfb24/iwwwfb24_00.pdf |archivedate=July 26, 2011}}</ref> In the same year, the "C.C. Mei Symposium on Wave Mechanics and Hydrodynamics" was organised at the International Conference on Ocean, Offshore and Arctic Engineering (OMAE).<ref>{{Citation |title=C.C. Mei Symposium on Wave Mechanics and Hydrodynamics |work=OMAE 2009 |url=http://www.asmeconferences.org/OMAE09/WaveMechanics.cfm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20110218022229/http://www.asmeconferences.org/OMAE09/WaveMechanics.cfm |archive-date=2011-02-18 |url-status=dead |publisher=[[American Society of Mechanical Engineers|ASME]] |accessdate=2011-01-15}}</ref>

He was inducted into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1986 for “application of the theories of wave hydrodynamics and elasticity to problems in coastal and ocean engineering.”<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Dr. Chiang C. Mei
 |url=https://www.nae.edu/27983/Dr-Chiang-C-Mei
 |website=National Academy of Engineering
 |access-date=13 April 2026
}}</ref>

==Death==
Mei died at his home in [[Waltham, Massachusetts]], on July 16, 2026, at the age of 91.<ref name="death"/>
